status: registered before any v5b score is computed; v5 outputs are retained unchanged
trigger: External review of the frozen v5 results (README section 3.6) identified one numerical defect and three inference weaknesses. All four were verified against the frozen code before this registration: (1) world5.py _predictive uses np.einsum('pr,rr,pr->p', V, sig, V), which reads ONLY the diagonal of the posterior covariance sig; the linear-Gaussian predictive variance is tau2 + V sig V^T with the full quadratic form. Reproduced: on a random positive-definite sig the diagonal-only form gives 1.99 where the full form gives 0.77 (and 8.88 vs 3.60 elsewhere) - the error is signed both ways and propagates into acquisition ordering, the precision blend and MI. (2) The precision blend prec = 1/bv + 1/pv mechanically returns a variance smaller than either channel although the template and the completion are fitted on overlapping training data; it is an uncalibrated fusion rule, not a Bayesian update, unless conditional independence holds. (3) The tau selection rule (decided >= 20 and wrong-rate point estimate <= 0.05) is empirical threshold screening: 0 wrong in 20 independent decisions has a Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95 percent upper bound of 0.139, not 0.05; calibration episodes are additionally correlated through shared templates and basis, so any UCB is optimistic in the known direction. (4) The v3/v4/v5 'oracle' arm uses BOTH the true readings (term matrix T) and the true label (it maximises the true class's margin); the v1-v5 headline gap therefore mixes response-prediction value with label access.

C1_variance_fix.change: world5b._predictive computes p_var = tau2 + einsum('pi,ij,pj->p', V, sig, V), the full quadratic form. Everything else in the world is unchanged.
C1_variance_fix.registered_expectation: The sign of the effect is NOT predicted. The fix changes the world predictive variance, hence rank selection, blend precision, acquisition order and MI values. Any v5 conclusion that survives is strengthened; any that flips is reported as flipped. The v5 section-3.6 mechanism note (precision blending shrinks variance and a margin-gaming planner exploits the tighter ranking) is downgraded to 'confounded with the einsum defect' and retested here.
C1_variance_fix.what_would_change_the_conclusion: If, with the corrected variance, at least one realistic arm reaches a finite tau_emp in any fold, the v5 'frontier does not move' claim is revised. If the tau-8 wrong-rate ordering between margin and MI reverses, the Goodhart-reduction claim for MI is revised.

C2_blend_variants.change: Three fusion rules for combining the class template (bm, bv) with the completion (pm, pv): (a) 'precision' = the v5 rule, now explicitly registered as an uncalibrated heuristic; (b) 'holdout' = convex mean mu = w*pm + (1-w)*bm with working variance w^2*pv + (1-w)^2*bv, where w in {0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0} is selected per fold by the same simulated-episode training log-likelihood machinery used for rank selection (one scalar per fold, selected on training compounds only, then frozen for calibration and held-out episodes; mirrors the rank-selection discipline, basis-leakage approximation carried over from protocol5); (c) 'off' = template only, run under the MI rule as the decision-level ablation of the completion channel.
C2_blend_variants.registered_expectation: If the completion channel carries real per-compound information, the holdout selection should pick w > 0 in most folds and the holdout arms should not be worse than 'off' under MI. If the v5 precision-blend gain was an artefact of double-counted evidence, holdout selects w at or near 0 or the off arm matches the blend arms.
C2_blend_variants.what_would_change_the_conclusion: w = 0 selected in all folds, or off_mi matching holdout_mi in correct rate, retires the completion channel at the decision level regardless of its predictive log-likelihood gain.

C3_oracle_decomposition.change: Two new ceiling arms, run as episode runners on the same term matrix T as the v3 oracle, with the same split-half calibration: (a) 'oracle_reading' sees T (all classes' true future terms) but NOT the label; it purchases the candidate whose realised update maximises the top1-top2 score margin (perfect response prediction, label-blind); (b) 'oracle_label' sees the label but NOT T; it purchases the candidate maximising the expected margin of the TRUE class over the best other class under the true class's own template predictive (7-point Gauss-Hermite-style quantile grid over N(val_m[truth,j], val_s[truth,j]^2)); it cannot see which lines lack readings, so it can be charged QC failures exactly like the realistic arms. The imported v3 'oracle' is renamed conceptually to 'oracle_full' (kept as arm name 'oracle' for comparability).
C3_oracle_decomposition.registered_expectation: oracle_full >= oracle_reading and oracle_full >= oracle_label by construction. The scientifically load-bearing contrast is oracle_reading vs oracle_label: if oracle_reading approximates oracle_full, the v1-v5 gap is mostly response prediction and a better world model is the right lever; if oracle_label approximates oracle_full while oracle_reading falls to near the realistic arms, the headline gap is mostly label access (choosing evidence to support the known answer) and the 'approach knowing the readings' wording in section 3.6 must be retracted.
C3_oracle_decomposition.what_would_change_the_conclusion: The v5 statement 'the compound-level accuracy needed approaches knowing the readings themselves' is retained only if oracle_reading stays clearly above every realistic arm.

C4_qualification_statistics.change: Every (arm, tau) cell additionally reports cp_ucb, the Clopper-Pearson one-sided 95 percent upper bound on the wrong rate. Two selection rules are reported side by side: tau_emp (v5-compatible: decided >= 20 and point estimate <= 0.05, renamed 'empirical qualification') and tau_ucb (strict: decided >= 20 and cp_ucb <= 0.05). The words 'certification'/'certified' are retired for point-estimate selection in all v5b text. The oracle arms' headline numbers are re-reported under both rules.
registered_limitations: cp_ucb treats calibration episodes as independent; they share templates and basis within a half, so the UCB is optimistic in the known direction (toward smaller bounds).
tau is calibrated on half-fold worlds and applied to full-fold worlds; threshold transfer is an assumption carried over from v2-v5 and NOT fixed in this block.

The strict tau_ucb rule with 20-decision minimum is nearly unattainable by construction (0/20 gives UCB 0.139 > 0.05); it is reported to quantify how far the current evidence is from certification-grade evidence, not as a practical gate.

controls: masked and shuffled variants of each new realistic arm (inherit the base arm's tau, as in v5)
imported_unchanged: planner_learned_thompson and their v5 controls - imported from the frozen v5 outputs for cross-run comparison
arms.genetic_tier: unchanged from protocol5 (gated on a finite tau_emp of a realistic arm; the channel fit is reported unconditionally). The gate is expected to fail; if it passes anywhere, the tier runs under the holdout-blend MI arm.

comparability: Episodes, folds, menus, budget 16, validator and tau grid are identical to v5. planner_precision_* differs from planner_learned_* ONLY through the corrected predictive variance (C1). All cross-run comparisons against v5 arms use the frozen v5 outputs.

gate_v5b.check_1: at least one new realistic arm reaches a finite tau_emp in at least one fold (v5-compatible rule)
gate_v5b.check_2: oracle_reading correct > best new realistic arm correct (the reading channel carries decision value above anything learnable so far)
gate_v5b.check_3: shuffled controls of every new realistic arm decide on <= 10 percent of episodes at their base arm's tau
gate_v5b.interpretation: check 1 failing reconfirms the v5 frontier under the corrected world; check 2 failing would mean even perfect response prediction does not open a decision gap, which retires the world-model lever on this task; check 3 failing invalidates the corresponding arm's margin as evidence, as in v5

reporting: README section 3.7 (measured vs v5, what survives); each claim tagged Measured / Proposed / Not established; the phrase 'empirical qualification frontier' replaces 'certification frontier' for point-estimate selection.
